source: No maker manual. Read from the panels, the CHANGELOG.md shipped in the installed plugin (v2.4.23), the literal pool and the C++ symbol table of the installed plugin binary, the port map we hand-read, and the community manual at https://github.com/patman023/nysthimanual, which is almost entirely empty. NYSTHI ships no presets and no demo patches.

The three panel sizes are one class with one port numbering, so the indices here are the same in all of them; the smaller panels simply place no widget for the sections above their own count.

complexSimpler.notes: Two jacks take polyphony. A polyphonic cable into the left record input sets the recording width from its channel count (0x34d800), and the speed CV input is summed across all its channels (0x34dd44). The left output carries those recorded voices back as channels (0x34e280). The record trigger is read only while one of the two record inputs is patched (0x34d730). The selection start CV is taken as an absolute value at 0x34cb1c, so a negative voltage moves the start the same distance as its positive twin.

lines: A programmable sequencer in the manner of the Roland MC-4. A sequence is built stage by stage, and finished sequences are stored as patterns that can be played one after another
Starts and stops the sequencer
A trigger starts and stops the sequencer
Returns the sequencer to its first stage
Sends a pulse each time the sequencer is reset
The rate of the internal clock
Passes on the clock the sequencer is running on
A clock here takes over from the internal clock
A pulse resets the phase of the internal clock, to bring it into step with something else
Switches pattern playing on and off, so the stored patterns are played one after another rather than the single sequence
Sends a pulse on each stage
A gate on each stage, as long as that stage's gate setting makes it
The note of the stage being played, as a pitch voltage
The second voltage of the stage being played
Sends a pulse when a pattern reaches its end
Note — each stage carries a note, a second voltage, a gate length and a length of its own
Note — NUM STAGES shows how many stages the sequence holds, and CURR STAGE is clicked to choose which stage the displays below it show
Note — NOTE sets the pitch the CV1 output carries for that stage, and can be set to REST for a silent stage
Note — CV2 sets the second voltage that stage carries
Note — GATE sets how much of that stage's length the gate output stays high for, as a percentage
Note — LENGTH sets how long that stage lasts, from 1/384 to 1/12 of a note, 1/16 to begin with
Note — NUM PATTERNS shows how many patterns are stored and CURR PATTERN is clicked to choose which one is loaded
Note — a new sequencer holds no stages and plays nothing: set the note, second voltage, gate and length on the displays, then add a stage with ADD STAGE, and repeat for each stage of the sequence.
Note — a sequence is stored as a pattern with ADD PATTERN, and pattern playing steps through the stored patterns one after another rather than the sequence being edited.
Note — with the mouse over the module the number keys type a value, and N chooses note entry, D length, G gate and C or V the second voltage
Note — with the mouse over the module, R sets the note to REST, keypad Enter adds a stage at the end, Return updates the current stage and I inserts one before it
Note — with the mouse over the module, Page Up and Page Down move between stages and Escape drops the edits to the current stage
Menu — SHOW RUNNING STAGE — keeps the displays following the stage and pattern being played
Menu — CONTINUOUS EDIT — writes each edit into the current stage as it is made, while the sequencer is stopped
Menu — TRANSPOSE — moves the whole sequence with TRANSPOSE +12, TRANSPOSE +1, TRANSPOSE -1 and TRANSPOSE -12
Menu — TRANSPOSE PATTERN +12 — moves the current pattern up an octave, with TRANSPOSE PATTERN +1, TRANSPOSE PATTERN -1 and TRANSPOSE PATTERN -12 beside it
Menu — STAGE COMMANDS — ADD STAGE, INSERT STAGE, UPDATE CURR STAGE FROM SCREEN, LOAD CURR STAGE TO SCREEN and DELETE STAGE, all acting on the sequence being edited
Menu — PATTERN COMMANDS — ADD PATTERN, INSERT PATTERN, UPDATE CURR PATTERN FROM SEQUENCE and LOAD PATTERN TO SEQUENCE, all acting on the stored patterns
Menu — EDIT — COPY SEQUENCE, CUT SEQUENCE, PASTE SEQUENCE and DELETE SEQUENCE act on a whole sequence
Menu — COPY CURR PATTERN — with CUT CURR PATTERN, PASTE PATTERN, DELETE CURR PATTERN and DELETE ALL PATTERNS, acts on the stored patterns
Menu — DELETE SEQUENCE — printed with (option/window key down) and carried out only with that key held, as is DELETE ALL PATTERNS

Note — right-clicking the wave display gives the editing commands: cut, copy, paste, delete, zero, invert, normalise, amplify, fades, trimming, and one undo of the last edit

Menu — TIME DISPLAY MODE — sets what the time display shows: Show Sample Length Time, Show Selection Length Time, Show Selection Length Samples or Show Playhead Time
Menu — PRE-RECORD MODE — records for a set length rather than until it is stopped, with PRE-RECORD TIME in SECONDS: taking a value from 0.5 to 120 seconds
Menu — Gate REC mode — switches the record command over to a gate
Menu — VISUALIZE STEREO, LEFT or RIGHT — on the wave display's menu, chooses which channels are drawn: Show STEREO, Show LEFT or Show RIGHT
Menu — Inverted Colors — on the wave display's menu, swaps the colours the wave is drawn in
Menu — TRIM Selection — on the wave display's menu, throws away everything outside the current selection
Menu — UN-TRIM Sample — on the wave display's menu, brings back what a trim threw away
Menu — RENDER Selection to Sample — on the wave display's menu, makes the current selection the whole sample
Menu — RESET Selection To MAX — on the wave display's menu, sets the selection to the whole sample
Menu — PEAK Threshold Level: — on the wave display's menu, sets the level a peak has to reach before the peak grid cuts there
Menu — PEAKs distance: — on the wave display's menu, sets the least distance apart at which two peaks are both cut at

lines: An additive oscillator: sixteen harmonics drawn as rotating vectors, each with its own magnitude, phase and frequency trim, summed into one wave
Sets the level of the summed output
The sum of all sixteen harmonics
The sum of the odd numbered harmonics
The sum of the even numbered harmonics
Sets how much of the voltage at the octave CV jack reaches the octave
A voltage shifting the octave, scaled by the OCTAVE knob
Sets the depth of linear frequency modulation from the LIN FM jack
A signal modulating the base frequency linearly, scaled by LIN FM
Sets the depth of exponential frequency modulation from the EXP FM jack
A signal modulating the base frequency exponentially, scaled by EXP FM
Sets the base frequency, 1V per octave
That harmonic on its own, at its own frequency, magnitude and phase
That harmonic on its own at a low frequency, for use as a modulation source; it carries 0V while Low Power Mode is on
Sets how far the voltage at that harmonic's magnitude CV jack moves its magnitude
A voltage moving that harmonic's magnitude, scaled by that harmonic's magnitude attenuator
A voltage moving that harmonic's phase
Sets how far the voltage at that harmonic's trim CV jack moves its frequency trim
A voltage moving that harmonic's frequency trim; with Frequency Trimmers as FM inputs switched on in the menu it modulates that harmonic's frequency instead
Raises the low harmonics against the high ones at one end of its travel, and the high against the low at the other
An attenuverter setting how far the voltage at the TILT CV jack moves the tilt
A voltage moving the tilt, scaled by the TILT CV attenuverter
Moves the magnitude of every harmonic up or down together
An attenuverter setting how far the voltage at the OFFSET CV jack moves the offset
A voltage moving the offset, scaled by the OFFSET CV attenuverter
Deletes every keyframe stored in the animator
Deletes the keyframe shown as the current one, and the values stored in it
Stores the screen as a new keyframe, reached over the time set as NEXT KF TIME
A trigger stores the screen as a new keyframe
Runs the animation through the stored keyframes, and stops it while it is running
A trigger runs the animation, and stops it while it is running
Pauses the animation where it stands, and carries on from there when pressed again
A trigger pauses the animation, and carries on from there
Sets a running animation back to its starting condition
A trigger sets a running animation back to its starting condition
Runs the animation over and over rather than stopping at the last keyframe
Note — each harmonic's magnitude is dragged on its bar, from -2 to +2, with the red line marking 1.0
Note — each harmonic's phase is dragged on its dial, from 0 to 360 degrees
Note — each harmonic's frequency trim is dragged on its dial and moves that harmonic away from exact harmonicity by -20% to +20%; right clicking it resets it to zero
Note — the sign row marks each harmonic as plus or minus, and right clicking it inverts that harmonic's frequency, which this oscillator can run negative
Note — BASE FREQ Hz sets the frequency the harmonics are built on and is dragged on its display; the octave beside it runs from -5 to +5
Note — the animator's displays read the number of stored keyframes, the length of the whole animation in seconds, and which keyframe is being shown
Note — CURR KF TIME is the time taken to reach the keyframe being shown, and NEXT KF TIME the time that will be given to the next one stored
Note — CURR KF TIME and NEXT KF TIME are set by clicking and dragging on them, with a minimum of 0.01 seconds
Menu — Set Harmonics ratio to standard tuning — works the sixteen frequencies out from the base frequency as the harmonic series
Menu — Set Harmonics ratio to square of position — with to cube of position, to square root of position and to Hammond B3 wheels, the other ways the sixteen frequencies are worked out
Menu — Low Power Mode — stops the low frequency copies of the harmonics, which then carry 0V, and saves what they cost to compute
Menu — Frequency Trimmers as FM inputs — turns each harmonic's trim CV jack into a linear FM input for that harmonic
Menu — Full Reset — returns every harmonic to the module's starting magnitude, phase, trim and sign
Menu — Reset to SAW — sets the sixteen magnitudes and phases to build a saw, with Reset to SQUARE and Reset to TRIANGLE beside it
Menu — Show Phasor — draws the rotating vectors, with Show Path drawing the path they trace and Show Wave the wave they make
Menu — Zoom IN — scales the drawing up, with Zoom OUT and Zoom Reset beside it
Menu — Randomize All Magnitudes — scatters the magnitudes across all sixteen harmonics, with Randomize All Phases, Randomize All Frequency Trimmers and Randomize All Frequency Sign beside it
Menu — Zero All Magnitudes — clears the magnitudes on all sixteen harmonics, with Zero All Phases, Zero All Frequency Trimmers and Reset All Frequency Sign beside it
Menu — Add 1 Random KF, Add 10 Random KFs and Add 100 Random KFs — build an animation of that many random keyframes, taking their range from the magnitudes of the first two harmonics
Menu — Load Current Frame To Screen — puts the values of the current keyframe onto the screen, and Save Screen To Current Frame writes what is on the screen back into it
Menu — Max AMP Harmonic — sets that harmonic's magnitude to full, with Half AMP Harmonic and Zero AMP Harmonic beside it, on the menu that harmonic's own column carries
Menu — Invert Frequency Sign — turns one harmonic's frequency negative, on the menu that harmonic's own column carries; the harmonic's number is printed after the name
Menu — 0 Phase Harmonic, 90 Phase Harmonic, 180 Phase Harmonic and 270 Phase Harmonic — set one harmonic's phase to that many degrees, on the menu that harmonic's own column carries

Jooper.notes: The polyphony is real and it is per channel: at 0xfd9ac each of the thirty-two signal inputs is added into its row's bus one channel at a time, using its own channel count, and at 0xfdcf4 the matching signal output is given the width of the widest input on that row. The switch, scene and expander jacks are all read as channel one only. Four of them — the two step jacks and the two that pair with them — count any voltage other than 0V as high, negative voltages included, so no threshold is written for those.

lines: A polyphonic wavetable oscillator. The table is navigated in two directions, by bank and by wave within the bank, and a swarm of detuned voices can be spread over both
The pitch, read at one volt per octave
Fine adjustment of the pitch
Shifts the pitch by whole octaves
A voltage shifting the pitch by whole octaves
Scales the exponential frequency modulation
A CV modulating the frequency exponentially
Scales the linear frequency modulation
A CV modulating the frequency linearly
Switches the swarm of extra detuned voices on and off
How far the swarm voices are spread in frequency
Scales the CV changing the swarm's frequency spread
A CV changing the swarm's frequency spread
How far the swarm voices are spread in pulse width
Scales the CV changing the swarm's pulse width spread
A CV changing the swarm's pulse width spread
How far the swarm voices are spread across the waves of the bank
Scales the CV changing the swarm's spread across the waves
A CV changing the swarm's spread across the waves
How far the swarm voices are spread across the banks
Scales the CV changing the swarm's spread across the banks
A CV changing the swarm's spread across the banks
Switches morphing on, so the sound blends between neighbouring waves instead of stepping from one to the next
Scales the CV changing the pulse width
A CV changing the pulse width
Scales the CV choosing which wave of the bank is played
A CV choosing which wave of the bank is played
Scales the CV choosing which bank is played
A CV choosing which bank is played
The output level
One of the two outputs carrying the oscillator
Note — a base table of 64 banks of 64 waves of 256 points is loaded when the module is created, so it sounds before anything is imported
Menu — MULTITHREADED — runs the oscillator on an extra thread; on macOS it starts switched off
Menu — LOAD BANK — reads a wav file into one bank slot; the slots are reached in groups of sixteen, under BANKS 0 --> 15, BANKS 16 --> 31, BANKS 32 --> 47 and BANKS 48 --> 63
Menu — LOAD GLOBAL BANK — reads in a whole set of banks saved as one file
Menu — SAVE ALL BANKS — writes every loaded bank out as one file, which is what a new module then starts from
Menu — REMOVE ALL BANKS — empties every bank
Menu — SWARMING VCOs COUNT — sets how many oscillators a swarm runs: 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 20 or 24 swarmers
Menu — PROCESSING BLOCK SIZES — sets the block the oscillator computes in, from 16 samples up to 2048 samples
Menu — POWER MODE — sets how hard the oscillator works: LOW POWER, MEDIUM POWER or HCF MODE
Menu — STOP GRAPHIC ANIMATIONS — switches the moving displays off
